In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating the mean-value function and generating realizations of a nonhomogenous Poisson process having trends and/or cyclic effects.
the problem of estimating and simulating the mean function of a non-homogeneous Poisson process with trends or asymmetric periodic components.
the development of a new method for estimating and simulating the mean-value function in the context of nonhomogeneous (nonstationary) Poisson processes with a long-term trend and/or cyclic effects.

the multiresolution-based nonparametric estimator of the mean-value process of a nonhomogeneously Poisson process is very effective in the presence of a long-term trend and/or cyclic effect(s) with asymmetric cycles.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a nonparametric approach that can be used to estimate and simulate nonhomogeneous Pois- son processes with long-term trends and cyclic effects, which may be of interest in many applications, including, but not limited to, modeling the arrival of calls in telecommunication networks.
we provide a method for estimating the mean-value function for a Poisson process with a long-term trend, and we present an algorithm to generate realizations of such a Poisson process.
we present a nonparametric method for modeling and simulating nonhomogeneous Pois-son processes that have a long-term trend with some cyclic effect(s).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the heuristic can be used for nonparametrically estimating the mean-value function and generating realizations of a nonhomogenous Poisson process having long-term trends or asymmetric cyclic patterns.
the multiresolution-based heuristic can be used to estimate and simulate Poisson processes with a long-term trend and cyclic effects that are asymmetric over their cycles.
